title: Fresh Blender 5.2 projective-motion holdout for the frozen Q30 curvature-risk candidate
question: On unseen opaque multi-owner Blender 5.2 scenes with new resolutions, material frequencies, rigid motion, camera parallax and same-index disocclusion, does the frozen D12.9-D1 Q30 previous-frame curvature candidate preserve useful history while bounding accepted bilinear reconstruction error?
decisionRole: confirmatory generalization test of the D12.9-D1 candidate; D12, D12.7 and D12.8 verdicts remain unchanged

requirements: Every fixture ID, raster, camera trajectory, owner trajectory, pass index, material coefficient, wave frequency, phase and formal path is unseen in D12.8 and D12.9-D1.
No D12.8 EXR, adapted array, mask, risk payload or per-pixel measurement may be a D12.9-H1 measurement input.
The Q30/Q24 formula, calibration factor, rounding allowance, thresholds, coverage gates, typed-depth domains and verdict mapping are frozen before any D12.9-H1 formal tool or render output exists.
Repeat 1 is primary; repeat 2 is an exact source, adapter, consumer and decision identity control.
A preflight may inspect Blender API, construct every scene without rendering and exercise synthetic branches, but may not create the formal root or emit a formal measurement.

sceneContract.construction: fresh factory state; opaque analytic tessellated rectangular surfaces with continuous Generated object-local emission; no source blend, image texture, light, transparency, deformation, simulation or external asset

surfaces.localPlane: local z=0 with rectangular bounds; the independent oracle intersects every declared surface and selects the nearest positive camera-depth hit

purpose: same Object Index on two analytic owners

projectionOracle.cameraConvention: Blender camera looks along local -Z; camera coordinates are transpose(R_camera_XYZ)*(world-cameraLocation)
projectionOracle.currentSurface: cast the current pixel-center ray through every declared bounded plane and select the nearest positive-depth hit; analyticOwnerId remains independent of Object Index
projectionOracle.previousSurfacePoint: inverse current owner transform maps the hit to owner-local coordinates; previous owner transform maps the same local point into world space
projectionOracle.predictedPreviousDepth: negative previous-camera Z of the transformed current local surface point
projectionOracle.independence: the analyzer implements scalar Euler XYZ, pinhole, bounded ray-plane intersection, visibility and rigid transforms without bpy, bpy_extras, mathutils or consumer imports

adapterContract.floatEncoding: little-endian finite float32 with no color transform
adapterContract.motion: vector.xy32 is current Blender Vector.XY exactly; consumer q=(x+Vector.X,y-Vector.Y); vector-next.xy32 retains current Vector.ZW for oracle validation
adapterContract.overwritePolicy: refuse if output directory or report already exists

validWhen: the current decoded owner and depth agree with the nearest analytic current surface
all four previous bilinear taps are in bounds
current alpha and all four previous tap alphas exceed 0.999
all four previous Object Index values equal current Object Index exactly
bilinearly sampled previous Depth matches transform-predicted previous-camera depth within max(1,predictedPreviousDepth)/1024
structuralValidity.sameIndexDepthRequirement: SAME_INDEX_DEPTH_CROSSING uses equal passIndex on two analytic owners so owner-only validity must expose wrong-history candidates and depth must reject them
structuralValidity.invalidFallback: every structurally invalid registered current pixel copies current float32 RGBA exactly
forbidden: owner-only acceptance in the same-index fixture
global depth epsilon not scaled by predicted depth
reading future or target RGB to decide structural validity

candidateContract.baseDomain: structurally valid AND current pixel and every current neighbor within Chebyshev radius 2 share current Object Index and alpha>0.999
candidateContract.support: the previous-frame 4x4 rectangle [x0-1,x0+2] by [y0-1,y0+2] is in bounds, has one exact Object Index and alpha>0.999
candidateContract.colorQ30: each previous float32 RGB sample multiplied by 2^30 must be an exact signed integer in the declared [0,1] domain
candidateContract.motionQ24: the fractional parts Fx,Fy of q=(x+Vector.X,y-Vector.Y), multiplied by 2^24, must be exact integers
candidateContract.curvature: Mx is the maximum absolute horizontal Q30 second difference at x0 and x0+1 on rows y0 and y0+1; My is the analogous vertical maximum at y0 and y0+1 on columns x0 and x0+1
candidateContract.accept: baseDomain AND support AND max(riskQ30.RGB)<=131072; comparison is inclusive
candidateContract.reconstruction: four-tap bilinear previous RGBA in y0x0,y0x1,y1x0,y1x1 order, explicit binary64 operation graph ((v0*w0+v1*w1)+v2*w2)+v3*w3 and one final float32 cast
candidateContract.fallback: registered current pixels outside accept, including structural, radius-2, support and risk rejection, copy current float32 RGBA exactly
subsetInvariants: accepted is a subset of supportEligible
supportEligible is a subset of radius2

validHistoryAgreement.domain: registered pixels independently classified VALID after owner, alpha, bounds and transform-predicted previous-depth checks

expectedDepthRejection.domain: registered same-index pixels for which owner-only validity would accept but transform-predicted previous depth exceeds tolerance

typedDepthDomains.aggregationRule: expected rejection pixels are never included in validHistoryAgreement maximum or sample count

identity: all parent file and internal hashes match
all Blender source repeats and canonical adapted arrays are byte-identical
Python and Node reconstructed, reason, mask and Q30 risk payloads are byte-identical
the independent analyzer exactly replays every payload and integer decision
all required child process IDs are unique and exit zero
producer reports contain no aggregate verdict
all registered mutation attacks are rejected

decision.supportedWhen: Every parent, freshness, runtime, process, source, adapter, projection, typed-depth, structural, Q30 identity, independent replay, risk conservatism, accepted quality, coverage, stress, static-control, fallback and audit gate passes.
decision.boundedWhen: All identity, projection, typed-depth, structural, risk-conservatism, accepted-quality, fallback, static-control, process and audit gates pass but any candidate coverage or curvature-stress gate fails.
decision.rejectedWhen: Any identity, projection, typed-depth, structural rejection, risk conservatism, accepted quality, fallback, static-control, process-totality or audit-totality gate fails.
decision.noRetroactiveRelabel: No D12, D12.7, D12.8 or D12.9-D1 label changes regardless of this outcome.

requirements: tamper a parent, runtime, tool, process, freshness or source identity
tamper an EXR, adapted array, report, typed envelope, result self-hash or evidence hash
flip Vector X sign, Y raster origin, pixel-center convention, Euler order or nearest-surface choice
swap analytic owners, pass indices, repeats or fixture identities
accept an out-of-bounds, wrong-owner, alpha-invalid or depth-invalid history pixel
merge expected depth rejection into valid-history depth agreement
alter Q30 or Q24 scale, second-difference support, maximum selection, calibration factor, ceil, allowance, saturation or inclusive threshold
read current RGB while making the candidate decision
alter explicit bilinear accumulation order or final float32 cast
flip support/radius/accepted subset or partition membership
hide an empty moving owner behind aggregate coverage
alter quality, coverage, stress, static-control, fallback or operation-count gates

diagnostics.integrity: every diagnostic is bound to source and payload hashes but is never a measurement input

nonClaims: D12.9-H1 does not revise any earlier negative or bounded result.
It covers only opaque rigid bounded planar owners with compiler-known transforms and Object Index/depth metadata.
It does not prove finite second differences upper-bound arbitrary rendered signals.

It does not validate curved surfaces, deformation, skinned characters, transparency, Cryptomatte fractional coverage, hair, particles, volumes, motion blur, depth of field or noisy path-traced lighting.
It does not establish temporal denoising quality, perceptual stability, cinematic quality, character consistency, production rendering or cross-platform GPU equivalence.
A supported result authorizes only the next preregistered geometry/material-domain expansion, not deployment.
